title: Hyundai delays its in-house autonomous driving solution to 2029
source_used: Motor Illustrated (citing Reuters and Korea JoongAng Daily)
key_facts: Hyundai's in-house autonomous driving software, Atria AI, is reported to arrive about two years later than planned; until then the group relies on Nvidia's platform.
Hyundai's press release talks about acceleration, while Reuters and the Korea JoongAng Daily report a choice to slow down.
The JoongAng quotes Park Min-woo, described as a Nvidia veteran, saying he made a strategic decision to slow down because rushing to mass production would risk a mediocre Level 2++ system.
His predecessor, Song Chang-hyeon, who focused on in-house software, left the post abruptly in December.
Level 2++ is not an official SAE level; Reuters describes it as a city assist comparable to Tesla's supervised FSD, and the driver remains responsible.
Hyundai's demonstration showed an Atria test vehicle driving in Seoul-area traffic; Hyundai does not say how many times a human had to take over.
Kwon Jung-hyun says 2027 is for polishing driving and safety, 2028 for edge cases, and 2029 for preparing safety certification in Korea, North America and Europe.
The first Nvidia Hyperion 10 vehicles will go without lidar, according to Reuters quoting Park.
quote_evidence: Reuters and the Korea JoongAng Daily instead report a choice to slow down its in-house software, Atria AI, which would arrive about two years later than planned.
The press release talks about acceleration.
Hyundai does not say how many times a human had to take over, or over how many kilometres.
why_it_matters_hint: A big carmaker is postponing its own driving software and leaning on Nvidia for now.
event_date: Delay first reported by Reuters on 14 Sep 2026 (search listing); this piece published 9 Oct 2026
notes: Late secondary account: search listings show Reuters ('Hyundai Motor to roll out in-house driver-assist system in 2029') and Quartz on 14 Sep 2026 and Yonhap on 13 Sep 2026. Motor Illustrated's piece includes the author's personal Tesla remarks and Canadian-market comments, not used. Presentation date at 42dot not stated.
